chambers_usher.text: Welcome to the City Chambers, on George Square. Queen Victoria opened it in 1888, and Glasgow has been showing off since.
Marble, mosaic, a great staircase and more gold leaf than a jeweller's. Merchants of the Second City of the Empire liked to flex.
Mind your manners on the stairs. The councillors are used to being looked at. You, however, may gawp.

then.text: Count everything on both sides, and sleep on it. That's my whole career in a sentence.

else.text: I get this every week. 'My rent's £800 and a mortgage would be £900, so I should buy.' Shall we look at that?

options: The deposit, repairs, insurance and being tied down

then.text: Hold on. A mortgage is not the whole bill.
Right. You'd need a deposit (often 5 to 10 per cent of the price or more), fees, insurance and a repair fund, and you can't leave in a month.
The postcode matters, but not for this sum.

else.text: Renting is flexible, and the landlord fixes the boiler. Buying builds equity, the part of the home that's yours, but you carry the risk, and interest rates move. A fixed deal holds yours for a few years, then you remortgage.
Neither is simply right. It depends on how long you'll stay, what you can save, and whether the sums still work when rates rise.
Oh, and in Scotland 'offers over' means the asking price is a floor, not a ceiling. People get caught out. Take some tablet. A grateful tenant left it.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
